the Tween-ether treatment of Rauscher virus (RLV), a murine leukemia, results in disruption of the virion, releasing the nucleoid.
Tween-ether treatment readily produced disruption of Rauscher virus, releasing a dense nucleoid and a capsid-like structure.
the structure of Rauscher virus, as determined by electron microscopy and by physical measurements, is different from that of the myxoviridae.

the study of the structure of RLV.
a study of the structure of the RLV and of its disruption.
the elucidation of the structure of RLV, and the comparison of this virus with other types of virus.

Rauscher leukemia virion is composed of a lipid envelope, an outer capsid, an inner shell containing the nucleic acid, and a nucleocapsid core.
the structure of RLV is similar to that of myxovirions.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the outer shell of immature virions of RLV is a capsid made up of a helical structure and is not a lipid envelope, while the inner shell of the mature virons is a helical structure made up of nucleic acid and protein.

The main takeaway from our work is that

RLV, a type-C virus, shares some morphological and physical properties with type-A myxovirues, such as the presence of an internal component, the release of the nucleocapsid after Tween-ether treatment, the buoyant density of 1.18 gm/ml of the internal component, and the release of a nucleocapsid with the same diameter as that of NDV.
the outer shell of RLV may represent a capsid, and the inner shell a nucleocapsid, as in other types of virus such as myxovirions.
the Rauscher murine leukemia virus is a myxovirus, with the same type of nucleocapsid as NDV and influenza virus.
